title: Calling it: the most valuable thing AI did for my trading was tell me no. Now I need your brains.
author: Ok_Map5721
selftext:
Everyone's posting AI agents that optimize strategies while they sleep. Mine did the opposite.

I gave it one job: try to kill every strategy I had.

Not "make it better". Not "find the best parameters". Kill it. Count every version I tried. Measure the real costs instead of trusting my config. Check if the test could even see an edge. Run the whole thing on random noise first.

It killed almost everything.

224 candidate setups went into an honest walk-forward. Zero came out.

My favorite result, a t-stat of 16.9, turned out to be the same 12 hours counted 144 times. Real number: 1.28.

Six of my "predictive" features found patterns in pure random data.

7 out of 12 of my "this doesn't work" conclusions were also wrong, because the test was too weak to see anything either way.

And a slippage number I'd typed in months ago and never checked was off by 5.5x.

So where am I now? I've got a bot that's honest. It doesn't bleed money, because it refuses to trade anything that doesn't pass. But it doesn't make money either. All the plumbing works: data, execution, risk limits, and the testing pipeline that kills bad ideas. What it's missing is something worth trading.

That's where you come in.

I'd like to run a proper brainstorm here. If you're a sane person who's been around long enough to be skeptical, drop your ideas below. Doesn't have to be a finished strategy. A market you think is still inefficient, a data source most people ignore, a mechanism that might pay retail for doing something others won't. Even "here's why X can't work" is useful.

My side of the deal: I'll run the promising ones through the same brutal tests and post what happens, good or bad, so everyone learns. And if something actually turns into money, I'm open to sharing with whoever brought the idea.

One rule: fairy tale sellers and shovel sellers, please scroll past. No courses, no signal groups, no "my bot made 300% last month", no tools you happen to sell, no "DM me". If your idea only works when someone pays you first, it's not an idea, it's a business model.

Ideas in the open only. What would you test?

comments.author: Individual-Quote-958
comments.body: The t-stat dropping from 16.9 to 1.28 after fixing the overlapping windows is such a good catch, most people never correct for that. If you want something to point it at, I'd try short horizon moves around scheduled events like earnings or CPI, since the timing is known ahead and you can build clean placebo dates. Funding rate extremes on crypto perps are another one where the mechanism is at least plausible. Would love to see the results either way.

replies.author: Ok_Map5721
replies.body:
Thanks, both are exactly the kind of thing I was hoping for.

Funding extremes: I've actually poked at that one already. As a straight predictor my test was too weak to say anything either way, and a rotation version (long low funding, short high funding on smaller perps) died on costs, about +5bp/day gross against \~14bp of costs. So I'd only revisit it with a different angle, maybe extremes only, not a constant rotation.

Scheduled events I like a lot, for exactly the reason you said. Known timing plus placebo dates is a clean design. The catch with CPI is sample size: 12 releases a year means only a couple hundred independent events even with a long history, so the detection threshold gets big fast. Earnings are more promising on that front, since you get thousands of events across stocks, as long as you cluster by date, because a lot of them land in the same weeks.

Going on the list. Will post results either way.

replies.author: _koenig_
replies.body: nice! I'm also building something similar. Right now I'm finishing random universe comparisons. I'll remember to plug in t-stat as well.

replies.author: Ok_Map5721
replies.body:
Nice, random universe comparisons are underrated. Most people only compare against zero, not against what a random pick of the same assets would have done.

One tip on the t-stat: compute it on date-clustered returns, not per trade. If a lot of your trades or events land in the same weeks, the per-trade t-stat will look much better than it should. And keep a running count of every variant you try, so you can deflate for it at the end.

If you want to compare notes once it's done, feel free to DM me.
